title: unified-metering-for-partial-message-resets-and-batched-retries
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Background: We've observed inconsistent token crediting when streaming sessions issue mid-stream 'reset' or when client libraries perform batched retries (re-sending fragments with dedupe tokens). The billing pipeline currently ties final token credits to a session terminal event; intermittent resets and partial-message aborts sometimes leave provisional credits in limbo leading to under- or over-charging.

Goal: Implement a single, deterministic metering flow that handles: (1) partial-message resets (client requests to truncate last N tokens), (2) batched retries where duplicate fragments are submitted with idempotency keys, and (3) reconnects that resume from a non-terminal frame. Ensure final token attribution matches the canonical committed transcript and surface transparent audit records for investigations.

Scope: runtime-serving hooks + metering-collector + billing-finalizer. This ticket focuses on the correctness rules and implementation plan; downstream billing adjs and customer-facing refunds handled by ENG-118800.
acceptance_criteria: Final credits equal the canonical transcript token count for 1000 randomized streaming sessions (coverage includes: mid-stream reset, batched-retry of last 2 fragments, reconnect-resume at offset, and interleaved client messages)
No double-credit events observed when duplicate fragments are submitted with same idempotency key (end-to-end test)
All streaming sessions produce an immutable commit_marker in the metering stream; finalizer uses the latest commit_marker to close accounting
Integration tests added: streaming_sim harness + billing-simulator validates credits and refund flags
Latency impact of additional commit markers is < 2ms median per request path in canary (runtime-1.23 canary)
proposed_solution:
1) Introduce a lightweight commit_marker frame that runtime emits whenever a session applies an explicit 'truncate' or when the server decides to commit a partial batch. commit_marker contains: sequence_number, canonical_offset, idempotency_bucket, and cumulative_token_count.
2) Metering-collector will treat commit_marker as the single source-of-truth for final token attribution for that session segment. Provisional token records remain until a commit_marker acknowledges them.
3) On reconnect/resume, the runtime includes last_seen_sequence_number and last_commit_marker_id so collector can trim or backfill provisional entries deterministically.
4) Batched retries must carry client-provided idempotency keys; collector dedupes by (session_id, sequence_number, idempotency_key).
5) Billing-finalizer reconciles commit_markers by monotonic sequence_number and writes a compact audit row: (session_id, final_commit_id, final_token_count, final_timestamp). This row is what billing consumes for invoicing.

Trade-offs: commit_marker increases event volume modestly but centralizes correctness and simplifies downstream reconciliation. Alternative (not chosen): make finalizer algorithmically reconstruct transcript using full frame logs — expensive and brittle under reordering.

Open decisions: format of idempotency_key header (uuid vs hash) and retention window for provisional records (suggest 24h).
tech_notes: Runtime changes: emit commit_marker for three events: explicit client 'truncate', server-side flush after >512 token provisional buffer, and session close
Collector changes: add idempotent upsert path keyed by (session_id, commit_id). Maintain provisional table with vector clock for sequence_numbers
Finalizer: run reconciliation job that consumes commit_marker stream and closes sessions where final_commit_marker observed or where tombstone seen
Metrics to add: commit_marker_emitted_count, provisional_record_size_bytes, commit_latency_ms_p50/p95, dedupe_hits
Backwards compatibility: old sessions without commit_marker should fall back to existing close-event logic for 90 days
test_plan: Unit: dedupe logic for (session_id, sequence_number, idempotency_key) with randomized arrival order
Integration: streaming_sim with 10k sessions — scenarios: mid-stream truncate, duplicate fragments, reconnect/resume with out-of-order frames
E2E: billing-sim validates invoice-level totals vs canonical transcripts for a 7-day synthetic workload
Performance: canary rollout to 3% of traffic and run latency/cost comparison against control cluster
Chaos: inject lost frames and simulated clock-skew to validate monotonic sequence handling
